Key Research Thinking Patterns: Topological Realization via Symmetry Contradiction: Proving non-existence of group actions by constructing finite-order symmetries that violate compact support constraints on infinite type surfaces (e.g., Markovic’s Minimal Decomposition Theory applied to Big Mapping Class Groups).

Metric Construction via Thermodynamic Potentials: Defining path metrics on moduli spaces by analyzing the Hessian of pressure functions and spectral gaps of transfer operators to establish real-analyticity and non-degeneracy (e.g., Construction of Weil-Petersson Path Metrics using Lasota-Yorke Type Estimates).

Cross-Domain Dictionary Extension: Generalizing correspondences between Kleinian groups and rational maps to higher-dimensional holomorphic dynamics and fixed-point-marked spaces (e.g., Extending Sullivan's Dictionary to Fixed-Point-Marked Rational Maps and CP^k).

Spectral-Geometric Correlation Analysis: Linking geometric properties of Julia sets, such as volume dimension and Hausdorff dimension, to spectral invariants like the correlation of multiplier spectra and pressure function zeros (e.g., Manhattan Curves in Complex Dynamics linking geometry to spectral proportionality).
Summary Description: Yan Mary He is a mathematician specializing in geometric topology and complex dynamics. She bridges infinite-dimensional group theory with the metric geometry of dynamical systems. In topology, she utilizes Markovic’s decomposition and symmetry analysis to resolve realizability problems for big mapping class groups on infinite type surfaces. In complex dynamics, she pioneers the analytic theory of Blaschke products and rational maps, extending Sullivan’s Dictionary to higher dimensions. Her work constructs Weil-Petersson and Manhattan metrics on moduli spaces via thermodynamic formalism, proving real-analyticity of dynamical invariants through spectral gap analysis and pressure function zeros. This research rigorously links geometric convexity and volume dimensions to spectral correlations, advancing the understanding of non-uniformly hyperbolic systems.
